title: The Perceptron
hook: The 1958 perceptron was the first algorithm that learned its own weights from examples — the seed of everything, and the model whose limits sparked the first AI winter.
key_points: Rosenblatt's perceptron (1958) is a single linear classifier that learns from data.
It adjusts weights whenever it misclassifies an example, until it separates the classes.
Minsky & Papert (1969) showed one layer can't learn XOR — a famous limitation.
Stacking perceptrons into layers, trained by backprop, became the neural network.
content_html: The perceptron, introduced by Frank Rosenblatt in 1958, was the first machine that learned its own decision rule from examples instead of being programmed by hand. It takes a weighted sum of its inputs and fires if the sum crosses a threshold — a single artificial neuron — and it updates those weights every time it gets an answer wrong. It is the historical and conceptual seed of modern neural networks.
extra_html:
How it works

For each training example the perceptron computes a weighted sum of the inputs and outputs one of two classes. When it misclassifies, it nudges the weights toward the correct answer. If the two classes can be separated by a straight line (or hyperplane), this simple rule is guaranteed to find such a boundary. That "learn from your mistakes" loop prefigured how all later models train.

Why it matters

The perceptron's fame is double-edged. Its success fueled early optimism about machine intelligence, but in 1969 Minsky and Papert proved a single perceptron cannot even learn the XOR function, helping trigger the first "AI winter." The resolution — stacking perceptrons into layers and training them with backpropagation — is exactly the multi-layer network at the heart of deep learning today.

related.hook: A neural net learns by asking, for every weight, 'how much did you contribute to my mistake?' Backprop answers all of them at once.

flashcards.prompt: What famous limitation of a single perceptron did Minsky and Papert show?

choices.text: It cannot learn the XOR function
It cannot be trained on labeled data
It requires more than two inputs
